messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph).
• In cities: 25–35 mph.
• Rural roads: 55 mph unless posted otherwise. | Speed limits can be lower in construction zones or school zones. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑seat or booster.
• Children under 4 must be in a rear‑seat child‑seat. | Failure to buckle up can result in a $50 fine. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Violations can lead to a $50 fine and points on the license. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, possible jail time. | Texas has a “zero‑tolerance” law for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02 %). | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right yields.
• Stop signs: stop, yield to pedestrians and traffic.
• School buses: stop when lights are flashing. | Failure to yield can result in a $50 fine and points. | | **Headlights & Lighting** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Fog lights are allowed only in fog or heavy rain. | Failure to use headlights can lead to a $50 fine. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must display valid registration stickers.
• Towing a vehicle requires a valid permit. | Unregistered vehicles can be towed and fined. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in fire lanes, handicap spaces (unless you have a permit), or on sidewalks.
• Parking meters and municipal lots have posted times. | Violations can result in a $50 fine and towing. | | **Points System** | • Traffic violations accrue points.
• 4 points in 12 months → license suspension.
• 6 points in 24 months → license suspension. | Points can be reduced by attending a driver improvement course. | | **Commercial Driver’s License (CDL) Rules** | • Separate set of regulations for commercial vehicles.
• Hours of Service (HOS) limits apply. | Violations can lead to license revocation and heavy fines. | | **School Bus Laws** | • Drivers must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Must remain stopped until the bus’s stop sign is retracted. | Failure to stop can result in a $500 fine and points. | | **Pedestrian & Bicycle Rights** | • Pedestrians have the right of way at crosswalks.
• Bicyclists must ride in the direction of traffic. | Failure to yield to pedestrians can lead to a $50 fine. | | **Emergency Vehicles** | • Drivers must pull over to the right and stop when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches. | Failure to yield can result in a $500 fine. | ### How to Find More Detailed Information 1. **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Official rules, statutes, and penalties. 2. **Texas Transportation Code** – Full legal text. 3. **Local County or City Ordinances** – May have additional restrictions (e.g., speed limits, parking). Feel free to ask if you need specifics on a particular law or how to handle a particular situation!
